title_en: A First Phone Is Too Early at Eight
title_ru: Первый смартфон в восемь лет — это слишком рано
description_ru: Рассуждение о том, в каком возрасте ребёнку стоит давать смартфон, с примерами из жизни и советами для родителей.
text:
When should a child get a first mobile phone? This question is very popular in my country, and it is often the reason for arguments in my family. My little cousin is eight years old, and she already has a smartphone. In my opinion, this is much too early. I think children should wait until they are at least twelve or thirteen.

Let me start with my own experience. I got my first phone when I was fourteen. It was an old, small phone that could only make calls and send messages. I was a little embarrassed, because my classmates had better ones, but now I am very grateful. I spent my time with friends, I played football and I read many books. I could not watch videos all day, because my phone simply could not do it.

Today, a smartphone is almost like a small computer. It has games, videos, social networks and thousands of applications. These things are made to be interesting, and they are very difficult to stop. Adults often use their phones too much, so imagine how hard it is for a child. My cousin plays games for three or four hours a day. When her mother asks her to stop, she gets angry and sometimes even cries. That is not healthy. Last month she forgot to do her homework three times, and she told her teacher that she was too tired. Her mother was very worried, and she took the phone away for a weekend. It was a difficult weekend for everybody in the house, but my cousin finally went outside and played with the neighbour's children.

The first danger is for health. Doctors say that children need to sleep for nine or ten hours, but many of them take their phones to bed. The light from the screen makes it harder to fall asleep. As a result, they are tired at school, and they cannot concentrate. Looking at a small screen for a long time is also bad for the eyes, and children who sit all day do not get enough exercise. A boy in my class wears glasses now, and his mother thinks the phone is the reason.

The second danger is on the internet. A young child cannot always understand what is safe and what is not. He can see violent pictures, talk to strangers or read cruel messages from other children. Bullying is easier online, because people are braver when they do not see the face of the other person. A friend of mine had a very bad experience when she was twelve. Some girls wrote unkind things about her in a group chat, and she did not want to go to school for a week. A child needs to be older and stronger to deal with this.

Many parents tell me that they buy a phone because they want to know where their child is. This is a good reason. Parents worry, and a phone can help them feel calmer. Some children also need to call home after school or when the bus is late. I agree with this. But for this purpose, a simple phone is enough. It is cheaper and safer than a smartphone, and it has no internet.

Of course, phones can also be useful. Modern children use them to find information, to learn languages and to make videos. My younger brother learned to draw with a free application. Phones can connect families who live far from each other. I do not want to say that technology is bad. It is a tool, and every tool is good or bad depending on how we use it.

That is why I think that parents should set clear rules. First, there should be no phones at the dinner table, and no phones in the bedroom at night. Second, there should be a time limit for games and videos. Third, parents should talk to their children about the internet and show them how to stay safe. And parents themselves should be a good example. It is hard to say "put your phone away" when you look at yours all evening.

Some parents say that it is impossible to refuse, because every child in the class has a phone. I understand the pressure. But if several parents talk to each other and agree to wait, the children will not feel alone. In conclusion, I believe that a childhood without a smartphone is longer, calmer and happier. There is plenty of time for screens later. Right now, children need friends, books, sport and sleep more than they need another application.

focus_sounds.tip_ru: Губы округлите и вытяните вперёд, зубы не касаются губы. Это не русское «в».
Верхние зубы касаются нижней губы, звук звонкий. Не заменяйте на русское «в» с округлением губ или на «w».
Спинка языка касается мягкого нёба, звук идёт через нос. Не добавляйте «г» в конце.
Звонкие согласные в конце слова (b, d, g, v, z) не оглушайте: say «bed», а не «bet».

questions.question: How old does the writer think a child should be for a first phone?
questions.answer: At least twelve or thirteen years old.

questions.question: What was the writer's first phone like?
questions.answer: It was an old, small phone that could only make calls and send messages.

questions.question: What are two dangers of smartphones for children?
questions.answer: Bad sleep and health problems, and unsafe things on the internet such as bullying.

questions.question: What rules does the writer suggest?
questions.answer: No phones at the table or in the bedroom at night, time limits and talks about internet safety.
